newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai IPOs seen wallowing despite market rebound.
newsitem.headline: Thai IPOs seen wallowing despite market rebound.

text.p: Thailand's initial public offer market is expected to remain sluggish as issuers keep to the sidelines due to an uncertain stock market outlook and lingering fears over the health of the economy, bankers said on Thursday.

"We have to see another few weeks before advising our clients' to float their IPO shares. The market direction remains unclear and various negative factors still exist," Napalak Waisiriroaj, head of investment banking at Thaimex Finance and Securities, told Reuters.
After tumbling close to five-year lows last week on a crisis of confidence in the economy, Thai stock prices have rebounded sharply this week as the crisis begins to fade.
By late on Thursday the key Stock Exchange of Thailand share market index was barely changed at about 716 points, after plunging to 676.65 last week.

The market has been supported by government plans for a bond issue of up to 100 billion baht ($3.87 billion) to prop up the battered property market, into which banks and finance firms have poured a huge portion of their loans.
But most issuers and bankers were cautious about the market's upswing, and questioned whether the rise would be sustained.

Last week's slide in share prices reflected a range of economic concerns, including a crisis among finance firms and a possible downgrade of Thailand's long-term foreign debt rating by Moody's Investor Services, analysts said.
"We think the IPO market may be dull until the third quarter," said Napalak.
According to the Securities and Exchange Commission, the value of funds raised through IPOs in 1996 climbed to 87.64 billion baht from 62.04 billion the previous year.
Only a handful of small issues have been launched since the second half of last year when the bourse began tumbling from heights of around 1,300 points.

"We are closely monitoring the situation in the stock market. If sentiment continues to improve and investor interest returns, we may start launching some IPOs," said Ekachai Techaviriyakul, head of investment banking at IFCT Finance and Securities.
Bankers said demand for new public offerings was very low among investors, many of whom were focusing instead on the market's large number of low-priced shares.

For example, Submicron Technology Plc, a unit of Alphatec Electronics Plc, has put its IPO issue on hold indefinitely and is finding other options to raise funds for the construction of its new production facility.

"We all know that the stock market is not very good. We will get a very low IPO price if we decide to float the shares now," Safina Komoltamaetee, public relation manager at Alphatec Electronics, told Reuters.
Submicron, Thailand's first semiconductor foundry, had hoped to be listed on the stock exchange by the first quarter of this year.
